digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate — file-impact scoping and attestation validity
propositions: Empty file_impact today is ambiguous between 'author forgot' and 'no files touched', causing conservative whole-HEAD invalidation and container poison rules that produce false churn for genuinely file-less tickets.

A tri-state file_impact_scope (undeclared, paths, none) with explicit no_file_impact_reason field makes the distinction clear: undeclared tickets still trigger whole-HEAD fallback and poison rules; none-declared tickets do not invalidate on unrelated commits and do not poison container drift scope.
An explicit none declaration becomes part of the material fingerprint so attestations invalidate on scope change, preventing retroactive widening of validity after signing.
A dedicated plan-review criterion judges the correctness of no-file-impact assertions against the plan, firing only when the assertion is present.
A container inherits the union of path-declaring children only, with none-declared children treated as neutral (neither contributing nor poisoning the inherited scope).
